claim_en: The breath-construct נִשְׁמַת (nishmat, 'breath of') stands in the Torah in EXACTLY TWO places - Genesis 2:7, the forming of the human, and Genesis 7:22, the flood's dying - and Bereshit Rabbah 14:10 joins them by the verbal analogy it calls chayim-chayim ('life'-'life'), ruling the soul-terms interchangeable. The machine confirms the pair is unique: both verses carry the same three elements, נִשְׁמַת ('breath of'), חַיִּים ('life'), and בְּאַפָּיו ('into his nostrils').

The BARE compound name יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים (YHWH Elohim, 'the LORD God') - the personal name followed by the unsuffixed generic - stands in the Torah in exactly twenty verses: nineteen across Genesis 2-3, the Eden narrative, and Exodus 9:30 alone outside it. Bereshit Rabbah 13:3 gives the rule for its debut at our 2:4 - שֵׁם מָלֵא עַל עוֹלָם מָלֵא (shem malei al olam malei, 'a complete Name over a completed world') - and Bereshit Rabbah 12:15 reads the compound as mercy mixed with strict justice, like hot water with cold, so the world endures.

The phrase נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה (nefesh chayah, 'a living soul') stands in the Torah exactly eight times, ALL of them in Genesis: 1:20, 1:24, 1:30 (the creatures), our 2:7 and 2:19, and 9:12, 9:15, 9:16 (the covenant after the flood). Our 2:7 is the only seat where it is prefixed - לְנֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה (le-nefesh chayah, 'INTO a living soul') - the human entering the category the swarms already held. Taanit 22b:11 reads the phrase at our verse as a COMMAND, not a description: R. Yosei forbids self-affliction by fasting because 'the soul I placed within you - keep it alive'. Bereshit Rabbah 14:9 types the five names of the soul on the same verse, with נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh) identified as the BLOOD (Deuteronomy 12:23).

תּוֹלְדוֹת (toledot, 'generations'), the section-header word our 2:4 debuts, is read as a CLASS MARKER on what it heads: whatever has generations 'dies, decomposes, is created but does not create'. The header therefore types its own subject as mortal - and our verse applies it, uniquely in the corpus, to the heavens and the earth rather than to a person.

check.note: Interpretive class-typing. Rides the standing DB-verified census of thirteen toledot seats in Genesis (lemma 8435) and standing claim G08-01's spelling finding - our 2:4 is written FULL where the other twelve run defective.

claim_en: Our 2:4's chiasm - the header's הַשָּׁמַיִם וְהָאָרֶץ ('the heavens and the earth') answered by the date-line's אֶרֶץ וְשָׁמָיִם ('earth and heavens') - is read at a tannaitic seat as a deliberate equalizer. R. Shimon in Tosefta Keritot 4:7: everywhere the heavens precede the earth, but in this one place the order flips, teaching that THE TWO ARE EQUAL. Bereshit Rabbah 12:12 argues the same by the palace and ship analogies: they were created as ONE act. The machine's recorded spec-delta on this verse is thereby witnessed as intentional, not a defect.

check.note: Interpretive. Rides standing claim G08-07, which machine-checks the flipped order's adjacency.

claim_en: Our 2:6 mist, אֵד (ed), is read as the world's ORIGINAL irrigation regime, later reconsidered and replaced by rain from above for four stated reasons. The chain thus records a spec change on the machine's own precondition state. Mekhilta DeRabbi Yishmael, Tractate Shirah 2:4 then shows the flood generation WEAPONIZING this very verse - 'we need Him not even for rain; a mist rises from the earth' - and being answered measure for measure with water from above (Genesis 7:12).

Resh Lakish derives the SUKKAH-ROOF specification from it - thatch must be insusceptible to impurity and grown from the ground, just as the mist arises from the earth. And the Jerusalem Talmud reads Adam as the BLOOD of the world from the same verse, handing the niddah commandment to the woman - the first of the three commandments the tradition assigns her.

claim_en: Two recorded disputes sit on our 2:8 planting. WHEN: מִקֶּדֶם (mikedem) is read not as 'in the east' but as BEFOREHAND - the garden planted on day three, before the human of day six (Bereshit Rabbah 15:3) - against Pesachim 54a:10, which reads it mi-kodem, the garden created BEFORE THE WORLD, one of the seven pre-creation things. WHAT CONTAINS WHAT: the machine models the garden inside Eden, and the containment relation is itself disputed - R. Yehuda holds the garden the larger, R. Yosei holds Eden the larger (Bereshit Rabbah 15:2). Both carried dual-track; the modeled parent edge stands.

claim_en: The machine flags our 2:11-14 river geography as known-geography - places named before they existed. source: Sanhedrin 56b:4; Bereshit Rabbah 16:6; Pesikta DeRav Kahana 12:1; Sanhedrin 56b:23
claim_en: THE CROWN OF THIS UNIT. R. Yochanan derives the commandments binding all humanity word by word from our 2:16 declare-operator: צַו (tzav, 'command') yields the ban on idolatry; יְהוָה (YHWH) blasphemy; אֱלֹהִים (Elohim) the duty of courts; הָאָדָם (ha-adam, 'the man') bloodshed; לֵאמֹר (lemor, 'saying') the forbidden relations; and מִכֹּל עֵץ הַגָּן ('of every tree of the garden') robbery. Pesikta DeRav Kahana 12:1 extends it into an accretion ladder - six to Adam, the limb-from-the-living added for Noah, and onward to Sinai. The count is itself disputed and the dissent is recorded: R. Yehuda holds Adam was commanded on idolatry ONLY, R. Yehuda ben Beteira adds blessing the Name, others add courts (Sanhedrin 56b:23).

check.note: Six laws read off one operator's own words, with the count carried as a recorded dispute.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 19:8; Bereshit Rabbah 19:3; Sanhedrin 29a:34; Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 4:1:9
claim_en: The death-penalty handler our 2:17 installs appears never to fire - the human eats and does not die that day - and the chain resolves it three ways on the operator's own wording. SCOPE OF THE DAY: 'you do not know whether one of My days or one of yours; I will grant him one of Mine, a thousand years' (Psalms 90:4) - so the handler DID fire, Adam dying at 930, inside the divine day. EXACT PAYLOAD: the prohibition was on EATING only; the touching clause is the woman's addition at 3:3, and on this exact gap Sanhedrin 29a:34 mints the legal principle כָּל הַמּוֹסִיף גּוֹרֵעַ (kol ha-mosif gorea, 'whoever adds, subtracts') - the fence built taller than the law is what the serpent pushed against. MOTIVE ON RECORD: the serpent is quoted reasoning FROM our clause - 'I know He said on the day you eat you shall die; I will trick them and they will be punished'.

check.note: Handler firing semantics, exact payload scope, and a recorded motive - all read off one operator.

claim_en: THE TOKEN-ASSIGNMENT OF THE SEVEN-LAWS DERIVATION IS ITSELF A RECORDED DISPUTE, CARRIED BOTH WAYS. The Babylonian mainline assigns this verse's ויצו ('and He commanded') to the duty of COURTS — 'as it says: he will command his children... to do justice' (Gen 18:19) — and אלהים ('God') to the ban on IDOLATRY; R. Yitzchak teaches the INVERSION (ויצו idolatry, אלהים courts), and Bereshit Rabbah 16:6 — the crown claim G08-28's own source — stands on the inversion side. Same seven laws, same verse, two recorded wirings of two tokens. Seated from the Noahide exam (finding F-012, owner: 'seat f-012 through f-016'; the auto-seat rule given in the same breath).
